title: Invert Binary Tree
source: canonical Invert Binary Tree concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is the root node of a binary tree. Mirror it: every node swaps its left and right children, recursively all the way down. Return the root of the inverted tree. The TreeNode class is provided in the starter code.
constraints: the tree stays balanced enough that recursion is safe

examples.explanation: Every left child becomes a right child, level by level.
An empty tree inverts to an empty tree.

hints: Swapping one node’s children is trivial; the trick is doing it everywhere exactly once.
Any full visit works: recursion, a stack, or a queue.
Pop a node, swap its two child pointers, then push the children; finish when the stack empties.
solution: Visit every node once and swap its two child pointers; a stack or queue drives the visit. O(n) time, O(width) auxiliary space.
failureHint: hidden tests include a single node and trees missing various children
